explanation: Saudi Arabia's 2019 Public Decency Regulations explicitly list public displays of affection as a finable offence, alongside immodest dress and unauthorized photography, with reported fines in the range of roughly 50 to 6,000 riyals. This sits alongside a separate track of 2019-era social reforms that relaxed strict gender segregation in cinemas, concerts, and some mixed venues, so 'everything is gender-segregated' is no longer an accurate summary — but affection in public specifically remains a punishable decency violation.
local_tip: Keep any physical affection, including extended hand-holding, for private spaces regardless of marital status.

also_check.note: Public affection carries real legal risk, with past cases resulting in arrest and jail time, though enforcement is inconsistent.
PDA is common in cosmopolitan Istanbul but best avoided in more conservative or rural areas.
Public affection is uncommon and can draw uncomfortable looks even among young couples.
